notes.title: Update 1.3 - Replaced "Orbit" and "Focus" modes with a seamless mouse movement across windows, and fixed lots of bugs
notes.content:
It's finally here! This should fix a ton of bugs people are having.

- Removed "Orbit" and "Focus" mode. Instead, now there is a little bar above each window. You can hold left mouse on it to drag it around. You can also scale a window by clicking and dragging in the top left corner, and minimize a window by clicking in the top right corner. There is a little gear icon in the top-right next to the minimize button that lets you change capture rate and change between focus and capture modes for that window.

- You can seamlessly move your mouse from one window to another, which is what lets me get rid of "Orbit" and "Focus" modes. If you aren't focused on a window and you move your mouse over it, you can click on that window and it will bring focus to that window

- Screens should no longer show up as "white" - now this will remember the state of them and so when they come back up they will look the same

- Mouse sensitivity now works

- Lots of mouse bugs fixed - it should work very well for you now =)

- Desktop capture should be working well now. This allows you to open any program through the desktop window

- The windows will save their positions when you exit out

- Multiscreens now detects if you have your headset on or not, and will let you use your mouse freely if it is off



Known bugs:

- If a window is not in the top left corner of your screen weird things will happen to your mouse. When you focus on a window it will automatically move that window there so this shouldn't normally be a problem, but if you manually drag them when looking in the desktop capture things might be weird for that window until you move it back - or focus on a different window and then focus back. I keep them in the top-left corner of your screen so your mouse doesn't get stuck at the edge of your physical screen (if a window on your desktop is going outside your monitor)

- Similarly, sometimes if you grab the actual window top (not the custom multiscreens top but the actual window top) the mouse will get excited and spasm a little. Working on fixing this, for now once you click or move your mouse into another window that will be fixed. So the intended use is to not move windows and instead move them physically around in multiscreens using the bar up top.

- When you press ctrl-alt-delete the capture freezes. Working on a fix soon, for now you'll just have to restart multiscreens.

notes.title: Update 1.2 - Full desktop capture is working!
notes.content:
Sometimes it is nice to see your entire desktop, for example, for opening programs. There is now a new window that is your entire desktop :)

Because this doesn't work for some people (such as some Laptops and people with Windows 7) I autodetect if it works for you at the start and there's a little bar in the menu that should tell you whether or not you have that functionality. If anyone's program is crashing though let me know and I can make a way to manually disable it if that test isn't working for you.

I'm told this is the same API that BigScreen and Virtual Desktop use, and after lots of optimization it is running very quickly for me. So enjoy :)

notes.title: Update 1.1 - Added lots of things
notes.content:
So technically this has been a series of mini updates by user request, but I'll list the changes here for reference:

- There is now a 3D mouse sensitivity slider
- You can enable Antialiasing and Supersampling at various levels
- The entire world should start in front of you now (not behind you or to the side) anymore, and if needed there is now a "reset origin" button. You click it once, then click anywhere while looking forward to set that to your default forward position
- Customizable backgrounds. They'res a little hacky for now, but it at least work. What you do is go to

C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Multiscreens\Multiscreens Vive\Multiscreens_Data\background

(or Multiscreens Rift)

and you'll see 6 textures there - front, back, left, right, top, bottom. You can change these to whatever you want and they will render in Multiscreens :). I included some examples there from various places as well

notes.title: Release and update 1.0
notes.content:
Multiscreens is officially out!

Shortly after release by request I made two updates:

1. Added a mouse sensitivity slider for the 3D mouse
2. Added the option to change the render scale (supersampling) of your headset and to change the level of antialiasing
3. (hopefully) Fixed the issue where sometimes you would start behind or far away from the menu

notes.title: Update 0.5 - Orbiting mouse cursor is working!!
notes.content:
Blerg steam is being slow...

In the meantime, really the natural way to work with windows (even in 3D space) is to use your mouse. Before you had to use an Xbox controller or keybindings, which worked but was pretty awkward.

Now you can move windows with your mouse! Specifically you can enter a "mouse control" mode via looking at a button below you for about a second (or by pressing ctrl-~), and this begins capturing anything you do with your mouse so programs no longer see those clicks and such happening.

Instead you have a little cursor that you can move similar to a mouse that orbits around the portion of space that you can see. When you left click with this cursor on any window it will focus on that window. When you hold right click on a window you can "drag" it around, then scroll in and out to push it in and out. When you aren't grabbing if you point your cursor at a window you can scroll to make that window bigger and smaller.

You can also click the middle mouse button (also Y on the Xbox controller) to open the "edit" bar below a window. This has:

- A slider that lets you change the target capture rate of that window
- A bar that shows you the name of that window
- A button to toggle the window in screen capture mode or in default render mode
- A button to minimize that window (this hides it, typically used to get a window out of the way that you don't want to see)

So I mean I guess on the bright side, since Steam is being slow you'll see these features in the first release! Which I think will help make this more usable for people.

notes.title: Update 0.0: Implemented Capture Mode*
notes.content:
I know this isn't out yet, but I figure making progress towards my goals already can't hurt while it's under review.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/xO1CTr0.png]Here's a teaser of capture mode[/url]. The * is because ideally I'd like to use the Desktop Capture API and I have that implemented there is just a importing bug when trying to run it on other people's computers that I haven't been able to fix yet. 

However, until then I found another way to capture anything, including the entire desktop as you can see in that teaser picture. This lets you capture technically any window about as efficiently as you can capture the windows in non-capture mode :) (except the entire desktop capture which is a little slow, so I added the option to disable it if you want). It also works on Windows 7 which is a plus for some of you.

My code will autodetect if a window can't be captured with my typical method, in which case it will use capture mode. However this autodetect code isn't perfect so I also allow you to change between capture mode and regular mode per window as well.

The downside to capture mode is it only works if the window in capture mode is currently focused. When it isn't I simply freeze that window when it's in capture mode because otherwise you would start seeing other windows above them which is kinda gross XD. However for the most part you only really are actively working with the current focused window (unless you are watching a video or something) so it isn't too bad. And for most things my non-capture mode is able to capture things well, which can run videos while you are working in other windows.

Just thought I'd share cause I was excited about this one :)

You won't see this in the first release because it still needs a little polish, but it should be in an update shortly afterwards.

notes.title: Update -1.0, Changed Scale and Background
notes.content:
This is still in the review process, but there's already an update XD

I changed the background of the room to match the graphic theme of Multiscreens, you can see a teaser [url=http://i.imgur.com/PONC3lU.png]here[/url].

More importantly, I adjusted the default scale of the screens :). They used to be these massive things, but now they are about the size of a typical computer monitor which makes things seem more real. For example, if you are working in room scale, you can put a few windows on one side of the room and a few other windows on another side of the room and walk between them.

You can also resize them and the changed sizes are also remembered upon closing and opening Multiscreens.

Right now there is no Vive Controller support, and keyboard support via keybindings exist but in my opinion it's kinda gross, so at the moment using an Xbox controller works best.

I've been working a lot on getting you to be able to change focus and move the windows around using only your mouse which should make this more natural/usable for people, so hopefully that should be ready in a week or two.
